IBM.rationale: IBM presents a moderately attractive setup anchored by genuine fundamental positives — strong YoY revenue growth (+9.5%), robust cash generation ($5.17B Q1 OCF, highest Q1 FCF in a decade per management), and a defensible franchise in regulated enterprise hybrid cloud/AI. Valuation has compressed dramatically: P/E at 20.5x vs. a 1-year average ~43x, and earnings yield (4.9%) now exceeds the 10Y Treasury (4.34%), a rare crossover. However, material caveats temper conviction: (1) QoQ EPS collapsed -44.6% with wide operating margin variance (8.0%→15.3%→8.7%) suggesting earnings volatility rather than smooth trajectory; (2) the mainframe cycle (IBM Z +51%) is a cyclical tailwind that will normalize, exposing slower underlying software growth (11% vs. 14% prior quarter); (3) balance sheet leverage is elevated at 21.2% equity ratio with $66.4B debt post-Confluent; (4) macro headwinds (oil +64%, widening credit spreads, geopolitical deal delays) create near-term enterprise spending risk. The stock's -21.6% quarterly decline has partially priced these risks, and the beat-and-maintain selloff (-8% on 4/23) may represent a short-term overshoot. FedRAMP authorization (1 April) and watsonx $5B+ cumulative bookings provide credible near-term catalysts for federal AI adoption. Net: a defensible, cash-generative franchise trading at a meaningful discount to its own history, but with enough earnings volatility and cyclical risk to cap the score at mildly attractive rather than strongly so.
